newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-GOOSEN DEFIES WET CONDITIONS WITH SPARKLING START.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GOOSEN DEFIES WET CONDITIONS WITH SPARKLING START.

text.p: Retief Goosen began in spectacular fashion to take an early two-stroke lead in the weather-affected French Open on Thursday.
The 28-year-old South African holed out with his second shot at the par-four 10th, his opening hole, and followed up with four birdies to move to six-under-par after playing 10 holes.
At that stage he was two strokes ahead of Irishman Paul McGinley, who eagled the long 18th to be four-under after nine.
Among the players a further two strokes behind was Goosen's playing partner Argentine Eduardo Romero, fourth in last week's German Open on the European Tour.
Sandy Lyle of Scotland, making a rare diversion from the U.S. for a three-week run of European Tour events, bogeyed the 17th, his ninth, to drop back to one-under-par after eight holes.
Steady rain caused a three-hour delay to the start of the first round before Goosen produced his stunning start.
Briton Colin Montgomery, leading European Tour player for the past four years, was a late starter.
